## Thinking

**What this asset is for.** The home-screen icon for an iOS PWA that gets baked into SpringBoard once, at install, and never re-read. There is no "ship a fix later" for this one — it has to be right now. It also has to survive a circular/squircle crop for the maskable variant, which makes the brief's "central eighty percent, even margin on every side" a hard functional constraint, not a stylistic nicety.

**What the brief actually specifies.** `src/interfaces/@brand/visual.md` → "The mark and the icon" is unusually precise for this asset: the cube must be caught *mid-turn*, with its top layer twisted 45° out of alignment with the two layers below it, "breaking the silhouette into a clean interlocking step." That sentence isn't decoration — the app is literally named for this motion, and the spec elsewhere calls the frozen-quarter-turn grid "the atomic unit the app is named for." This is the one thing that would make this icon *Quarter Turn's* icon rather than any stock Rubik's-cube clip art.

**What I saw at full size.** A cleanly rendered, hard-edged, flat-shaded cube on true black — genuinely well executed as a render: crisp square stickers, no gloss/bevel/gradient, good contrast, no melted geometry or AI artifacts. But the top layer is flush and aligned with the two layers below it. The outer silhouette is a plain hexagonal cube outline with zero notches, zero step — a solved cube, not one caught mid-turn. There's a thin orange stripe and a thin green stripe along the seam where the top meets the sides, which reads as the model's attempt to gesture at "a different layer" using a flat color trick rather than actual offset geometry — it doesn't touch the outer silhouette at all. This is the brief's single most load-bearing instruction, and it's simply not there.

**What I saw small.** At 48px and 128px it reads fine as a bold, high-contrast, colorful block shape — legibility is genuinely one of this render's strengths and I want to say that plainly rather than let the other findings bury it.

**Where the checker and my eye agree.** `image-check.mjs` flags uneven margin bands (67/33/127/127px). I confirmed this by eye and it's real: the cube sits ~17px low of center vertically (top margin nearly double the bottom margin), and its bounding box is 75% of frame width but 90% of frame height — both off the specified 80%, and not symmetric. For an asset whose maskable crop depends on symmetric safe margins, this is exactly the kind of defect the checker exists to catch and I'd have flagged it independently even without the warning.

**Where I went further than the checker.** The checker can report dominant hexes and their nearest brand token, but it can't tell you a color is in the *wrong neighborhood* the way a human eye tuned to this palette can. I sampled pixels directly: the top face (#FBC501) is a decent match to Flare (ΔE 3.6, confirmed by the checker), and the orange sliver (#FE6701) sits close to Ember. But the blue face (#0A5EE4) is a deeper, more saturated blue than Cardinal's tuned Cobalt (#2E7BFF) — the checker itself matched it closer to the *other* palette's Cobalt Deep (#2A62E0, ΔE 4.7) than to this app's own default blue. The green sliver (#50A905) is a yellow-leaning olive/lime, roughly 45-50° off Verde's hue (147°) — nowhere near "spring green." The red face (#E51E25) is a flat fire-engine red, missing the magenta lean that gives Signal (#FA2F45) its crimson character. And Chalk white — one of only six specified sticker colors — doesn't appear anywhere in the visible geometry. Your suspicion #2 is correct: three of five visible hues drift toward generic saturated Rubik's-cube primaries, and the app's specifically retuned, luminance-corrected palette is not what's on screen. For an app whose entire visual thesis is "these six specific colors are correct on black," that matters on the single most repeated brand touchpoint the product has.

Both problems are real and independent. The missing offset/interlocking silhouette is the more severe one — it's a hard-gate-level subject miss, not a nice-to-have. The margin and color issues are serious but secondary.

## Result

### Verdict

**`dist/web/public/icon-b27d032c.png` — regenerate.** Score 23/32 (acceptable band by raw total), but the **wrong-subject hard gate is tripped** and overrides the total: the brief's defining feature — the top layer frozen 45° out of alignment, silhouette broken into an interlocking step — is entirely absent. That is a different subject than the one the brief specified (Quarter Turn's mark, not a generic Rubik's cube), even though the general object class (a cube puzzle icon) is right. This is not shippable as the pre-install master.

Attempt 1 of 3. Sidecar confirms this was a live generation (provider `codex`, model `gpt-image-2`, `ignoredParams: []`, size honored, no transparency requested or delivered) — nothing here is a provider limitation; it's a brief-following miss, so a sharpened brief is the right next attempt.

Shipping this now would be uncorrectable for anyone who installs before a fix.

- **P0 — Wrong subject: no offset top layer, no interlocking silhouette step.** The brief's central, product-naming detail — the top layer twisted 45° out of alignment, breaking the outline into a clean step — is completely absent. The delivered cube is flush and solved-looking; the outer silhouette is a plain hexagon with zero notches. - **P3 — Register reads slightly generic/toylike rather than "precision instrument."** The flat, hard-edged, no-bevel execution correctly follows the letter of the register spec, but the overall effect lands closer to mass-market puzzle-app clip art than the "severe, precise" object described in `visual.md`. Minor, and likely resolves on its own once the silhouette and color fixes land — not worth a dedicated brief change on its own.

Working well, worth keeping: the flat-shading craft (no gloss, no gradient, no watermark, hard square sticker corners) and small-size legibility (clean, high-contrast, reads at 48px) are both genuinely strong and the regenerated brief shouldn't disturb them.

### Brief edits

Replace the `icon-1024.png` brief block in `src/interfaces/@brand/visual.md` with:

> A 3D icon of a Rubik's-style cube frozen mid-turn, filling a full bleed square composition with no padding or margin, on a pure black background. The cube's entire top layer is twisted forty-five degrees out of alignment with the two layers beneath it: at each of the top layer's four corners a small triangular notch cuts into the outline and reveals near-black plastic underneath, and the outer edge of the object is a stepped, notched silhouette, never a plain straight-sided box.
